Anya: Quick sync - support reported customers saving a per-route view, then later surprised that console cost preview used the route's default model instead of the one they had selected in the UI.
Ravi: Is this 'selected in the UI' meaning temporary ad-hoc model select or the persistent pin in the route settings?
Anya: Ad-hoc selection in the query inspector when you saved the view. The save request only persisted filters + route id. No model info.
Noah: That aligns with current API: `POST /saved_views {route_id: 'nlp.extract', filters: [...]}` -> no model field.
Priya: Two problems: (1) users expect exact replayability (same model & sample rate) and (2) cost/quota previews are misleading.
Jules: We could do a few options: a) UI-only hint that says "this view was created with model X" (local metadata), b) expand saved view API to include optional model binding, c) store a separate immutable snapshot resource.
Ravi: I prefer b) but with clear compatibility rules. We need to define what happens if model X gets deleted or incompatible (quantization, arch).
Anya: Draft fallback choices: `route_default`, `nearest_compatible`, `use_latest_revision`, `reject_with_error`. Default = `route_default`.
Noah: Backend impact: adding model_id to saved_views is straightforward but we must version the API (v2). Migration needs to keep existing rows untouched.
Priya: For audits, we should also capture `pinned_sample_rate` and `pinned_quantization` (if user chose non-default). Those affect cost calc.
Jules: UX: show small pill on saved-view card: either "Pinned: gptj-v2" or "Uses route default". On hover, show cost delta: `pinned_price / route_default_price` and sample-rate badge.
Ravi: Security/permissions: allow org admins to disable model pinning per workspace. Also check that model visibility rules are respected when displaying pinned model name to another team.
Anya: Good call. Add `allow_model_pinning` flag on workspace settings. If false, UI should disable pin control and show tooltip.
Noah: API sketch (v2) suggestion: `POST /v2/saved_views {route_id: "nlp.extract", filters: [...], bindings: {model_id: "redwood/gptj-v2@2026-03-01", sample_rate: 0.2, fallback: "nearest_compatible"}}`
Priya: We should keep `bindings` optional and immutable after save to preserve replayability. If users want to update, create a new saved view or explicit "rebind" endpoint.
Jules: Migration: leave existing saved_views.rows as-is. On UI load, if no bindings, compute hint by reading historical run logs to show "likely used model: X" (best-effort) and offer migrate button.
Ravi: Rollouts interaction: if a model pinned is under canary rollout, the pinned view must either pin exact revision or indicate semantic pin. We need two modes: `exact_revision` vs `semantic_tag` (e.g., `stable` label).
Anya: Add `binding_type: "exact" | "semantic"` with default `exact`. For `semantic` we resolve at replay time according to routing policy + rollouts. Also expose resolution audit.
Noah: Telemetry: emit event `saved_view.bind.resolve` with fields: saved_view_id, binding_type, resolved_model_id, resolver_reason. Useful for debugging and cost attribution.
Priya: Console telemetry should also add a cost comparison snapshot at save time (store both pinned_estimate and route_default_estimate strings) so support can answer questions quickly.
Jules: UX roadmap: 1) next minor: UI hint (no backend change) + migrate CTA 2) next sprint: API v2 + server-side binding storage + migration job 3) follow-up: admin controls + semantic binding support.
CI-Bot: CI passed for branch feature/saved-view-bindings. PR: https://git.company/repo/pulls/911.
Ravi: I'll scope infra changes once Lex posts expected query volume for resolving semantic bindings.
Anya: Thanks team. Noah, can you add the swagger snippet + a compact migration plan in this thread? Then we'll triage into backlog. :thumbsup:
